Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well.

applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Deolali Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 107(E).—WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Deolali Cantonment Board for Digging and use of 


Bore Wells, 2024 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice vide Notice No. 210/PWS/E-6/3466, dated the 
287 December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 277 January, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 


28" December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 02" January, 2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 


the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 10, dated 
06" March, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 


Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006), the Deolali Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 
namely: — 


1. 


Short title and commencement. - (1) These regulations may be called the Deolali Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
Definitions. — (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires — 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5;

(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 


Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Deolali Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(1851) or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 

(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, 


education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (1) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (1) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval.

(3) Post the termination of the license, same will be required to be renewed. 


(4) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - (1) The 
applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for 
extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (1) Registration Fee for digging of new bore well or existing bore well shall be rupees two 
thousand while applying for new connection or as may be specified from time to time. 


(2) License renewal fees shall be rupees one thousand which is valid for two years. 


(3) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, the 
registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application 
by the user to the authority with a fee of rupees one thousand. 


(4) Extraction charges will be as under: — 


(a) Ground water extraction charges for Group Housing Society, from bore well: rupees five 
per one thousand liter or as may be specified from time to time. 


(b) Ground water extraction Charges for commercial or industrial purpose, from bore well: 
rupees ten per one thousand liter or as may be specified from time to time 


(5) In case of discontinuation of existing bore well (in case of drying), a fresh application seeking 
permission of digging for new bore well shall be submitted by the applicant and renewal fee or 
modification fee for the Bore Well be rupees three thousand. Applicant has to also ensure that the 
existing bore well is filled with sand properly and closed off before digging new bore well. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees ten thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. - The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 3(E)— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Pachmarhi Cantonment Board for Digging and 
use of Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. 55/Water 
Supply/4255-4265, dated the 20" March, 2024 for inviting objections and suggestions by 30" March, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 
20" March, 2024 and in the local newspapers on 220 March, 2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 0 dated 


the 07 May, 2024. 


OW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (4 of 2006), the Pachmarhi Cantonment Board hereby makes the following Regulations, 


namely: — 

6 Short title and commencement. - (l) These regulations may be called the Pachmarhi Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 
(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 

2. Definitions. — () In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 

(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 

(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 

(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 
Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 


extraction of ground water. 


“Cantonment Board” means the Pachmarhi Cantonment Board;

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(ISD) or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 
(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 
(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust,

education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24% September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - () 
The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the 
structure for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed;

registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (l) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees two hundred. 


(2) Charges for residential bore well for extraction above two thousand five hundred liters per day shall 
be charged at twenty five paisa per liter or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for commercial or industrial bore well for extraction above eight thousand liters per day 
shall be charged at fifty paisa per liter or as may be specified from time to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees five thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - () Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Sagar Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 115(E).—WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Sagar Cantonment Board for Digging and use of 
Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. Borewell-2023-1, 
dated the 307 December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 297 January, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was published on the website of the Cantonment Board on 30th 
December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 30th December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 28, dated 
27th February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006), the Sagar Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, namely.— 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These regulations may be called the Sagar Cantonment 
Board (Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. - (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006); 
(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 


Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the notification issued 
by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide notification number S.O. 
3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; 


(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for extraction of 
ground water. 


(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Sagar Cantonment Board; 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC.4] 


(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute (ISI) or 


International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 
(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 


(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, education 
institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car spa, beauty parlour, 
barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose mentioned in Annexure - VI to 
the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification 
number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. - The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 


appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 


whether — 

(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is potable 
or not; 

(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is affected; 

(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 


the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (1) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (1) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant.

(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the license at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 


about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - (1) The 
applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for 


extracting ground water, namely:— 
(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. - (1) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 


user to the authority with a fee of rupees one thousand. 


(2) Charges for residential bore well extraction above hundred liters per day shall be charged at rupees 
fifty per day or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for commercial or industrial bore well extraction above fifty liters per day shall be charged 
at rupees two hundred per day or as may be specified from time to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees two thousand or as 


may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user.

17. Water audit. - Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


18. Appeal.—(1) — Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order of the 


Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE

NOTOFOCATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 116(E).— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Shillong Cantonment Board for Digging and use 
of Bore Wells, 2024 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice vide Notice No. SHG/6/BOREWELL/, dated 
the 29" December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 28" January, 2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 
29" December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 30" December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections or suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 


the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 1, dated 
5 February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006), the Shillong Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 


namely:— 


1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These regulations may be called the Shillong Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. - (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires — 

(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006); 

(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 

(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the notification issued 
by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide notification number S.O. 
3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for extraction of 
ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Shillong Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute (ISI) or 
International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 

(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, education 
institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car spa, beauty parlour, 
barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose mentioned in Annexure - VI to 
the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification 
number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 

(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 


respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate 
and control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 
247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

10. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment 
Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. - The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 


whether — 

(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is potable 
or not; 

(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is affected; 

(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 


the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (1) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (1) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at 
regular intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. — 
(1) The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure 
for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the forms I and IT; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed.

Levy of fee. - (1) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees one thousand. 


(2) Charges for existing residential bore well extraction above hundred liters per day shall be charged at 
rupees two per kilo liters or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for commercial or industrial bore well extraction above fifty liters per day shall be charged 
at rupees four per kilo liters or as may be specified from time to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees five thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose.

rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 


time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. - Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - (1) Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board.

about the existence of bore well.

any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees five thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose.

functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to

contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user.

ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority.

S.R.O. l4(E)— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Pune Cantonment Board for Digging and use of 
Bore Wells, 2024 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Borad vide Notice No. 


CEE/Borewell/Byelaws/2023, dated the 0I“ January, 2024 for inviting objections and suggestions by 30% January, 
2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 0I* 
January, 2024 and in the local newspapers on 03" January, 2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and disposed, of vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. Nil dated the 0I“ 
March, 2024; 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (4! of 2006), the Pune Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, namely:— 


l. Short title and commencement. — (|) These regulations may be called the Pune Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. — () In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 
notification number 5.0. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 


Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Pune Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 


(ISD) or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO);

(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the license at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - () 
The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the 
structure for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed;

(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made

Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (l) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees twenty thousand. 


(2) Charges for existing residential bore well — The charges shall be based on the quantum of water 
being extracted per day or as may be specified from time to time.

Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees fifty thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - () Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Jhansi Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


S.R.O. l0(E).—WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Jhansi Cantonment Board for Digging and use of 
Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. Jhansi/Regulation of 
Digging of Bore Well/2023, dated the 307 December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 29" January, 
2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the Cantonment Board on 30" December, 2023 and 
in the local newspapers on 3[7 December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 09, dated 
29" February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (4l of 2006), the Jhansi Cantonment Board hereby makes the following Regulations, 
namely:— 


l. Short title and commencement. — (l) These regulations may be called the Jhansi Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. — () In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC.4] 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 


Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Jhansi Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(SJ) or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 

(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, 


education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. —The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (/) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant.

deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - () 
The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the 
structure for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (l) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees ten thousand. 


(2) Charges for existing residential bore well for extraction up to two hundred litre per capita per day no 
charge shall be levied. However in case of extraction of more than two hundred litre per capita per 
day charges shall be rupees seventy paisa per cubic meter or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for existing and proposed commercial or industrial bore well are as follows:-

Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees one Lakhs or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. - Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority.

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Kanpur Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


S.R.O. (E).—WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Kanpur Cantonment Board for Digging and use of 
Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. CBK/Engg/K-820, 
dated 28"December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 27"January, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 28" 
December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 297 December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 3, dated 
the 05" February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (4! of 2006), the Kanpur Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, namely:— 


l. Short title and commencement. - () These regulations may be called the Kanpur Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. — () In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the notification 
issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide notification 
number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; 


(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Kanpur Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(ISD) or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 

(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, 


education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 2020 
by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


3. Survey of existing bore wells. — (|) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence and 
average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


4. Survey of ground water available. —The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry of 
Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated.

Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — (|) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(B), dated the 24" September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (!) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the date 
of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. — ()The 
applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for 
extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 
by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for extracting 
the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor 


Levy of fee. — () If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees one thousand. 


(2) Ground water extraction charges for Group Housing Society from bore well: rupees fifty per day or 
as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Ground water extraction charges for Commercial or Industrial purpose, from bore well: rupees two 
hundred per day or as may be specified from time to time.

person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling the

Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test

ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - () Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command.

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 9th August, 2024 


59.0. 3243(E).— WHEREAS, a draft notification was published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, vide 
number S.O. 4893(E), dated the 0 November, 2023, inviting objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be 
affected thereby within the period of sixty days from the date on which copies of the Gazette containing the said 
notification were made available to the public; 


AND WHEREAS, copies of the Gazette containing the said draft notification were made available to the public 
on the 0" November, 2023; 


AND WHEREAS, no objections and suggestions were received from persons and stakeholders in response to 
the said draft notification; 


AND WHEREAS, the Kamlang Tiger Reserve is spread over an area of 783 square kilometers and is located 
in the Lohit District in Arunachal Pradesh; 


AND WHEREAS, the Namdapha National Park and Tiger Reserve is spread over an area of 2230.245 square 
kilometer out of which 985.235 square kilometer is core and 245 square kilometers is buffer zone, located in the 
Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh in the North Eastern part of India; 


AND WHEREAS, the Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary was notified as Wildlife Sanctuary vide notification 
number CWL//D/58/88/375-3250 dated the 8" October, !989 and was given the status of Tiger Reserve from the 6" 
September,206 vide notification number CWL/D/I59/204/680-78 and the Namdapha was notified as national park 
vide notification number CLW/8/83/5284-5360 and was declared as tiger reserve vide notification number NO FOR 
482/D-4/84 dated February, 987; 


AND WHEREAS, the Kamlang Wildlife Sanctuary has been added to the extension of Namdapha National 
Park, also a tiger reserve and holds a rich biodiversity ideally suited for the growth of various floral and faunal form; 


AND WHEREAS, the Namdapha National Park is the only protected area in the world which harbours four 
big cat species like leopard, tiger, snow-leopard and clouded-leopard and it is the largest protected area in the Eastern 
Himalayan Biodiversity Hotspot and in terms of area it is the 3" largest National Park in India and the area is also 
known for the extensive dipterocarp forests, profusion of orchids, ferns and lianas among the last great remote 
wilderness areas of Asia; 


AND WHEREAS, the major floral species found in and around Kamlang and Namdapha Tiger Reserve are 
Diptrocarpus macrocarpus (Hollong), Shorea assamica (Sal), Altingia excela (Jutli), Moras levigata (Bola), Dillenia 
indica (Outenga), Terminalia myriocarpa (Hollock), Toona ciliata, Cinnamomum cecidodaphnnae, Castanopsis indica 
(Higori), Canarium resiniferum, Duabanga grandifolia (Khokan), Dixoxylon hamiltonii (Banderdima), Cryptomeria 
penicyata, Eleocarpus genitrus (Rudraksh), Acer oblongum (Himalayan maple), Arudinagramini folia (Bamboo orchid 
Jetc.; 


AND WHEREAS, the Kamlang and Namdapha Tiger Reserves supports more than sixty faunal species, 
including Manis pentadactyla (Chinese Pangolin), Capricornis thar (Himalayan serow), Nycticebus coucang (Slow 
loris), Macaca assamensis (Assamese macaque), Trachypitchcus pipeatus (Capped langur), Cuon alpines (Wild Dog), 
Ursus thibetanus (Asiatic black bear), Lutra lutra (Common otter), Prionailurus bengalensis (Leopard cat), Pardofelis 
marmorata (Marbled cat), Panthera pardus (Leopard), Panthera tigris (Tiger), Panthera uncia (Snow leopard), 
Moschus focus (Black musk deer), Moschus chrysogaster (Himalayan musk deer), Muntiacus muntjak (Barking deer), 
Naemorhedus sumatraensis (Himalayan serow), Ratufa bicolor (Malayan giant squirrel), Callosciurus pygerythrus 
(Hoary-bellied squirrel), Dremomys lokriah (Orange bellied Himalayan squirrel), Petaurista petaurista (Common flying 
squirrel), Bandicota indica (Large bandicoot rat) and Hystrix brachyuran (Chinese porcupine) etc.; 


AND WHEREAS, the Namdapha Tiger Reserve conserves, protect and provides shelter to rare floral species 
such as Sapria himalayana, Pinus merkusii, rare faunal species such as Cuora mouhotii, Helarctos malayanus, Melogale 
species, Mustela flavigula, Aonyx cinerea, Prinodon pardicolor, endangered species such as Biswamoyopterus biswasi, 
Ailurus fulgens, Prionailurus viverrinus, Panthera tigris, Panthera uncia, Elephus maximus, Hoolock hoolock, Axis 
porcinus, Moschus fuscus, Moschus chrysogaster, Hadromys humei, Manis pentadactyla and threatened species such as 
Rhacophorus namdaphaensis, Otter (Lutrinae species);

environmental and biodiversity point of view and to prohibit industries or class of industries and their operations and

section (2) and sub-section (3) of section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 986 (29 of 986) (hereafter in this 
notification referred to as the Environment Act), read with sub-rule (3) of rule 5 of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 
986, the Central Government hereby notifies an area to extent ranging from zero to .92 kilometres around the 
boundary of Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Namdapha Tiger Reserve, in the State of Arunachal Pradesh as the Kamlang 
Tiger Reserve and Namdapha Tiger Reserve Eco-sensitive Zone (hereafter in this notification referred to as the Eco- 
sensitive Zone) details of which are specified in paragraph | , for the purpose of protecting and improving the quality of 
environment and preventing, controlling and abating environmental pollutions and takes the following measures, 
namely:-

2. Zonal Master Plan for Eco-sensitive Zone () The State Government shall, for the purpose of effective 
management of the Eco-sensitive Zone, prepare a Zonal Master Plan within a period of two years from the date of 
publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, in consultation with local people and adhering to the stipulations 
given in this notification for approval of the competent authority in the State Government. 


(2) The Zonal Master Plan for the Eco-Sensitive Zone shall be prepared by the State Government in such manner 
as is specified in this notification and also in consonance with the relevant Central and State laws and the guidelines 
issued by the Central Government, if any.
