MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Secunderabad Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the !2th August, 2024 
S.R.O. 26(E).— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for Secunderabad Cantonment Board for Digging and use 


of Bore Wells, 2024 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. SCB/SWW/Digging of 
Borewells/336, dated the 4" February, 2024 for inviting objections and suggestions by 23" February, 2024; 


AND WHEREAS the said notice was also published on the official website of the Board on 4" February, 


2024 and in the local newspapers on 5" February, 2024; 


AND WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 


the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 02, dated 
05 March, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 


Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006), the Secunderabad Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 
namely:— 


. 


Short title and commencement. — (|) These regulations may be called the Secunderabad Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
Definitions. — () In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 


Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Secunderabad Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(ISD or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 

(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, 


education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24% September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area.

Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. The 
exempted categories are as follows: 


(i) Individual domestic consumers in both rural and urban areas for drinking water and domestic uses. 

(ii) Rural drinking water supply schemes. 

(iii) Armed Forces Establishments and Central Armed Police Forces Establishments in both rural and 
urban areas. 

(iv) Agricultural activities. 

(५) Micro and Small Enterprises drawing ground water less than 0 cum/day. 


Whereas, apart from the above, the exemptions from seeking No Objection Certificate (NOC) to 
Group Housing Societies, Residential Welfare Associations (RWAs) and Residential Apartments for ground 
water extraction will be applicable. Further, the provision for installation of flow meters to the bore wells is 
not applicable to the aforesaid exempted categories. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the license at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - () 
The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the 
structure for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., 
report mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number 5.0. 3289(E), dated the 247 
September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed.

(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (l) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees five thousand. 


(2) Charges for existing residential bore wells for extraction of water have been exempted on par with 
Regulation no. 7. 


(3) Charges for commercial or industrial bore well for extraction above fifty liters per day shall be 
charged at rupees ten per Kilo liter or as may be specified from time to time. 


(4) Charges to obtain permission for digging of bore well within Cantonment area shall be rupees three 
thousand for colonies and rupees one thousand for Slums/Basthis or as may be specified from time 
to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees five thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. - Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - () Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

New Delhi, the !2th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 23(E).— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Kamptee Cantonment Board for Digging and use 
of Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. !70 dated the 
28"December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 27"January, 2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 28" 
December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 29"December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 43, dated 
3 March, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (4l of 2006), the Kamptee Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations 
namely: — 


l. Short title and commencement. — (|) These regulations may be called the Kamptee Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. — () In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 
(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 


Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 
Jal Shakti;

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 


(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Kamptee Cantonment Board; 


(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(ISD or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 


(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 


(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, 
education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number 5.0. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the license at 
regular intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board.

(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. Exclusive use of the ground water by Military forces or their 
dependents will not in usual course be levied charges for the discharge of their routine functions 
including training activities. However, any commercial activity shall be charged as per usual rates. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - () 
The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the 
structure for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (l) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees two hundred or as may be specified from time to time. 


(2) Charges for residential bore well for extraction above one thousand liters per day shall be charged at 
rupees five thousand per annum or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for commercial or industrial bore well for extraction above one thousand liters per day shall 
be charged at rupees ten thousand per annum or as may be specified from time to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees ten thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - () Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 


S.O. 3272(E).—Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways, S.O No. 5139(E) dated 01.12.2023, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, 
Section 3, Sub-section (ii) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) 
(hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intension to acquire the land specified in 
the Schedule annexed to the said notification for building (widening/four-laning, etc.), maintenance, management and 
operation of Sirhind to Mohali section as a Spur to IT City-Kharar-Kurali road NH 205-AG on the stretch of land 
from Km 0.000 to Km 28.140 in the District of Fatehgarh Sahib in the state of Punjab. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “The Tribune" (English), and 
“Punjabi Tribune (Punjabi)” both dated 09.12.2023; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 


And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose;

का.नि.आ. 124(अ).--बोरवेल की खुदाई और उपयोग के लिए नसीराबाद छावनी बोर्ड हेतु मसौदा विनियम, 
2023-24 को प्रकाशित किया गया था, 26 जनवरी, 2024 तक आपत्तियां और सुझाव आमंत्रित करने हेतु छावनी बोर्ड के 
नोटिस बोर्ड पर अधिसूचना संख्या एनसीबी/ईडबल्यूएफ/बोरवेल/2023-24/172, तारीख 27 दिसंबर, 2023 के तहत 
प्रकाशित किया जाएगा। 


और जबकि उक्त अधिसूचना बोर्ड की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट पर 27 दिसंबर, 2023 को और स्थानीय समाचार 
पत्रों में 28 दिसंबर, 2023 को भी प्रकाशित किया गया था ; 


और जबकि, उक्त तारीख से पूर्व जनता से प्राप्त आपत्तियों और सुझावों पर छावनी बोर्ड द्वारा विचार किया गया 
तथा उनका समुचित निपटान छावनी बोर्ड संकल्प संख्या 1, तारीख 27 फरवरी 2024 द्वारा किया गया | 


अब, अतः, छावनी अधिनियम, 2006 (2006 का 41) की धारा 204 की उपधारा (4) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का 
प्रयोग करते हुए, नसीराबाद छावनी बोर्ड निम्नलिखित विनियम बनाता है, अर्थात्‌: - 


1. संक्षिप्त नाम और प्रारंभ- (1) इन विनियमों का संक्षिप्त नाम नसीराबाद छावनी बोर्ड (बोरवेल की खुदाई और 
उपयोग) विनियम, 2024 है।

2. 


(2) ये राजपत्र में उनके प्रकाशन की तारीख से प्रवृत्त होंगे। 
परिभाषाएं.- (1) इन विनियमों में, जब तक कि संदर्भ से अन्यथा अपेक्षित न हो,- 
(क) “अधिनियम” से छावनी अधिनियम, 2006 (2006 का 41) अभिषरेत है;

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Nasirabad Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 
S.R.O. 124(E).— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Nasirabad Cantonment Board for Digging and 
use of Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. 


NCB/EWF/Borewell/2023-2024/172, dated 27" December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 267 
January, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 
27" December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 28" December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 
the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 1, dated 
27" February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006), the Nasirabad Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 
namely:— 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These regulations may be called the Nasirabad Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Definitions. — (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the 
notification issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC.4] 


notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of 


Jal Shakti; 

(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for 
extraction of ground water. 

(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Nasirabad Cantonment Board; 

(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute 
(ISD or International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 

(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, 


education institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car 
spa, beauty parlour, barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose 
mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to regulate and control ground water 
extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number 5.0. 3289(E), dated the 24 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. — The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is 
potable or not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is 
affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (1) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (1) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant.

deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the license at regular

(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - (1) 
The applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the 
structure for extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (1) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees twenty thousand. 


(2) Charges for residential bore well — The charges shall be based on the quantum of water being 
extracted per day or as may be specified from time to time.

Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees fifty thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. - The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user.

17. Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


18. Appeal. - (1) Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

को सील कर दिया जाएगा और पांच हजार रुपए तक या समय समय पर यथा विनिर्दिष्ट अनुसार फीस लगाई 
जाएगी। 


14. भूजल की गुणवत्ता का संरक्षण- आवेदक और भूजल के उपयोक्ता को सरकारी एजेंसी से हर तीन साल में जल की 
गुणवत्ता का परीक्षण कराना आवश्यक है जिससे कि यह सुनिश्चित हो सके कि जल पीने योग्य है अथवा नहीं तथा 
इसकी रिपोर्ट प्राधिकारी को सौंपनी होगी और यदि जल दूषित पाया जाता है तो उस जल का उपयोग पीने के 
लिए नहीं किया जाएगा। 


15. वर्षा जल संचयन- प्रत्येक आवेदक को यह सुनिश्चित करना होगा कि वर्षा जल संचयन संरचनाएं बनाई गई हैं तथा 
वर्षा जल संचयन का ध्यान रखा गया है और बोर्ड यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि वर्षा जल संचयन कार्यात्मक है तथा 
बोर्ड द्वारा समय समय पर इस आशय का सर्वेक्षण किया जाएगा। 


16. निषेधात्मक आदेश- यदि पता चलता है कि पानी दूषित है और मानव उपभोग के लिए हानिकारक है, तो 
प्राधिकारी उपयोक्ता को नोटिस जारी करके निषेधात्मक आदेश जारी कर सकता है। 


17. जल अंकेक्षण -प्राधिकारी समय समय पर जल अंकेक्षण करेगा और भूजल की उपलब्धता सुनिश्चित की जायेगी 
और भूजल में कमी की स्थिति में, प्राधिकारी द्वारा,निर्धारित निर्णय के अनुसार भूजल निष्कर्षण पर प्रतिबंध 
लगाया जाएगा।

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(BARRACKPORE CANTONMENT BOARD) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 
S.R.O. 121(E)— WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Barrackpore Cantonment Board for Digging and 


use of Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. B//5/I/Vol- 
III/15, dated the 287 December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 27" January, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 


28" December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 29" December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 


the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 01, the 
dated 06" February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 


Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006), the Barrackpore Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 


namely: — 


1. 


Short title and commencement. - (1) These regulations may be called the Barrackpore Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
Definitions. - (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the notification issued 
by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), 
dated the 247 September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; 


(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for extraction of 
ground water. 


(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Barrackpore Cantonment Board; 


(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute (ISI) or 
International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO);

(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 


(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, education 
institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car spa, beauty parlour, barber 
shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to 
regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 
247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24% September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 


and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. - The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 


appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. - (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 


whether — 

(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is potable 
or not; 

(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is affected; 

(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 


the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24"" September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (1) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (1) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the license at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board.

Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. - (1) The 
applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for 
extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report

registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for extracting the

Directions by Cantonment Board. - The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. - (1) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees one thousand. 


(2) Charges for residential bore well extraction above hundred liters per day shall be charged at rupees 


one and fifty Paisa per kilo liter or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for commercial or Industrial bore well extraction above fifty liters per day shall be charged 


at rupees three per kilo liter or as may be specified from time to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees five thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 


shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 


time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. - Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority.

NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the !2th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 22(E).—WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Cannanore Cantonment Board for Digging and 
use of Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. Bore well/Bye 
laws/2023, dated the 28" December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 27" January, 2024. 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 
28" December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 29" December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 


the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 22, dated 


274 March, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 
Cantonments Act, 2006 (4l of 2006), the Cannanore Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 


namely: — 


l. Short title and commencement. - (l) These regulations may be called the Cannanore Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024.

(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
Definitions. - (l) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (4] of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the Cantonment 
Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the notification issued by 
the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide notification number 8.0. 3289(E), 
dated the 247 September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; 


(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for extraction of 
ground water. 


(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Cannanore Cantonment Board; 


(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute (ISI) or 
International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 


(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 


(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, education 
institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car spa, beauty parlour, 
barber shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose mentioned in Annexure - VI to the 
guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 
3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2)The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and 
control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 
September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (.) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 
and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment 
Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. - The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — () The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 
whether — 


(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is potable or 
not; 


(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is affected; 


(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 
the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board.

Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — () The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (.) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant. 


(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a 
deemed approval and for every new bore well, applicant shall be required to renew the licence at regular 
intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. — () The 
applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for 
extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed; 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24" September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for 
extracting the water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 
Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. — (l) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees one thousand. 


(2) Charges for average extraction of ground water per day for existing/proposed residential bore well 
shall be at the following rates on a monthly basis or as may be specified from time to time.

Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee which shall be based on the 
quantum of extraction, by adding ten per cent to the actual cost of extraction of water if sold for residential 
purpose and twenty per cent if sold for commercial purpose. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 
shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 
time. 


Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


Appeal. - () Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

New Delhi, the !2th August, 2024 
S.O. 3265(E).— In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section () of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for 
building (widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, management and operation 


of NH75Ext in the stretch of land from Km. l6.400 to Km. 2.340 in the district of RANCHI in the state of 
JHARKHAND, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section() of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, CALA, Ranchi in writing and shall 
set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard, either 
in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and after making such further enquiry, if 
any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be 
final. 
The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(Department of Health and Family Welfare) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the !2th August, 2024 


S.O. 3284(E).— Whereas, the Central Government in exercise of the powers conferred by section 26 A of 
the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 940 (23 of 940) prohibited the manufacture for sale, sale and distribution for human 
use of drug fixed dose combination of Etodolac + Paracetamol vide notification number S.O. 4706 (E), dated the 
7" September, 208, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, sub-section (ii), dated the 
7 September, 208; 


And Whereas, the said notification was challenged by M/s. Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd. in W.P. (C) 
No. 0098/208 before the High Court of Delhi, claiming that fixed dose combination of S(+) Etodolac + 
Paracetamol is not covered under the notification; 


And Whereas, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has passed judgement dated 22™ January, 2020, the operative 
part of the which is reproduced below:- 


“This court is of the view that the Impugned Notification, in so far as it is stated to be applicable to the FDC 
of S(+) Etodolac + Paracetamol cannot be sustained. The same is set aside. The matter is remanded back to 
DTAB/Sub-committee constituted by it to examine the issue regarding the said FDC in accordance with the directions 
issued by the Supreme Court in Pfizer Limited and others (Supra). The DTAB/Sub- Committee shall submit its report 
to the Central Government who may act thereon in accordance with law.”; 


[भाग ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 3 


And Whereas, the Drugs Technical Advisory Board in its 88th meeting held on 26" September, 2022 
deliberated the issue and recommended for constitution of a DTAB Sub- committee to examine the matter in light of 
the judgement passed by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court; 


And where as, the DTAB Sub-Committee considered the said fixed dose combination as irrational and 
recommended for its prohibition in public interest under section 26A of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 940; 


And Whereas, based on the recommendation of DTAB Sub- committee, matter was further deliberated in 
90th meeting of Drugs Technical Advisory Board held on dated 25" January, 2024 and made recommendation for 
prohibiting the manufacture, sale and distribution for human use of fixed dose combination of S(+) Etodolac + 
Paracetamol; 


Now, therefore, on the basis of the recommendations of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board and in exercise 
of powers conferred by section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 940 (23 of 940), the Central Government 
hereby prohibits the manufacture for sale, sale and distribution for human use of drug fixed dose combination of S(+) 
Etodolac + Paracetamol with immediate effect as the said drug is found to have no therapeutic justification and may 
involve risk to the human beings.

किसी भी रूप में बेचा नहीं जाएगा और यदि यह पाया गया कि आवेदक या कोई व्यक्ति बिना अनुमति निष्काषित 
भूजल को बेच रहा है, तो दी गई अनुमति को तत्काल निलंबित कर दिया जाएगा और बोरवेल तथा फ्लो मीटर 
को सील कर दिया जाएगा और दस हजार रुपए तक या समय-समय पर यथा विनिर्दिष्ट अनुसार फीस लगाई

इसकी रिपोर्ट प्राधिकारी को सौंपनी होगी और यदि जल दूषित पाया जाता है तो उस जल का उपयोग पीने के

MINISTRY OF DEFENCE 
(Aurangabad Cantonment Board) 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 


S.R.O. 120(E).—WHEREAS, the draft regulations for the Aurangabad Cantonment Board for Digging and 


use of Bore Wells, 2023-24 was published, on the Cantonment Board’s Notice Board vide Notice No. CBA/Bore 
wells/2023-24, dated the 287 December, 2023 for inviting objections and suggestions by 27" January, 2024; 


AND, WHEREAS, the said notice was also published on the official website of the Cantonment Board on 


28" December, 2023 and in the local newspapers on 29" December, 2023; 


AND, WHEREAS, objections and suggestions so received from the public by the Cantonment Board before 


the said date were considered by the Board and suitably disposed of, vide Cantonment Board Resolution No. 18, dated 
127 February, 2024. 


NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) of section 204 of the 


Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006), the Aurangabad Cantonment Board hereby makes the following regulations, 
namely: — 


1. 


Short title and commencement. - (1) These regulations may be called the Aurangabad Cantonment Board 
(Digging and Use of Bore Wells) Regulations, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of publication in the Official Gazette. 
Definitions. - (1) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,— 
(a) “Act” means the Cantonments Act, 2006 (41 of 2006); 


(b) “authority” means the Cantonment Board or the Chief Executive Officer authorised by the 
Cantonment Board under regulation 5; 


(c) “availability and use of water” shall have the same meaning assigned to it in the notification issued 
by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on Per Capita Availability of Water vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), 
dated the 247 September, 2020 issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti; 


(d) “Bore well” includes tube well or dug well or tunnel well or such other structures for extraction of 
ground water. 


(e) “Cantonment Board” means the Aurangabad Cantonment Board; 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC.4] 


(f) “flow meter” means the flow meter as per the standards of the Indian Standards Institute (ISI) or 
International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO); 


(g) “form” means the form annexed to these regulations; 


(h) “use of water” means usage of water by residential unit, house, bungalow, society, trust, education 
institution, industry, hotel, commercial restaurant, tea stall, coffee shop, spa, car spa, beauty parlour, barber 
shop, marriage grounds or halls etc., or for any other purpose mentioned in Annexure - VI to the guidelines to 
regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 
247 September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


(2) The words and expressions used in these regulations and not defined shall have the same meaning as 
respectively assigned to them in the Act, rules made there under, and in the guidelines to regulate and control 
ground water extraction in India issued vide notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24% September, 
2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Survey of existing bore wells. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct a survey of existing bore wells 
within its jurisdiction and the survey shall include the date from which the said bore wells are in existence 


and average extraction of water every day. 


(2) The density of the population shall be considered along with the availability of the present water 
supply source for considering the application for extraction of ground water within the Cantonment Area. 


Survey of ground water available. -The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey of the area within its 
jurisdiction to ascertain the level of ground water available for use with the help of agencies of the Ministry 
of Jal Shakti or any other organisation of the State Government in which the Cantonment Board is situated. 


Appointment of authority. - The Cantonment Board may appoint Chief Executive Officer to exercise the 
powers and discharge the functions and duties as an authority in such manner as may be specified in the 
appointment order. 


Preservation of natural water course. — (1) The Cantonment Board shall conduct survey to ascertain 


whether — 

(a) the drinking water is free from contamination as per the standards and whether the water is potable 
or not; 

(b) any source of effluent and hazardous water has percolated and water of the bore well is affected; 

(2) Taking into consideration the existing supply of water, quality, use and availability of ground water, 


the application for digging bore well shall be considered by the Cantonment Board. 


Exemption from permission for ground water extraction structure. — Exemption shall be granted by the 
Cantonment Board as per the guidelines to regulate and control ground water extraction in India issued vide 
notification number S.O. 3289(E), dated the 24"" September, 2020 by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 


Registration of existing bore wells. — (1) The authority shall publish a notice by giving wide publicity for 
compulsory registration of the existing bore wells, within a period of one month. 


(2) The form shall be issued to the residents for registration and the registration or renewal charges, if 
any, shall be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


Registration of new bore wells — (1) The applicant (owner, head of residence, lessee, legal heir, authorised 
occupant) may submit the application with the authority for digging new bore well in the specified form and 
the said application shall be scrutinised by the authority preferably within a period of thirty days from the 
date of application and the decision shall be communicated to the applicant.

(2) In case, the decision is not communicated within a period of thirty days, it shall not be treated as a

intervals as may be specified by the Cantonment Board. 


(i) The depth of bore well in the Cantonment area is restricted to sixty meters as applicable to the 
draught prone area and the same shall be extended in case of bore well used for extraction of drinking water. 


(ii) The size of bore well is permitted up-to six inches (fifteen cm) used for extraction of drinking water. 


(3) Military establishments within the local limits of the Cantonment Board shall be required to inform 
about the existence of bore well. 


Documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for extracting ground water. — (1) The 
applicant shall submit the following documents for registration or permission to erect the structure for 
extracting ground water, namely:— 


(i) The application and declarations as per the form annexed: 


(ii) Impact Assessment Report for a specified purpose issued by the concerned authority i.e., report 
mentioned in Annexure - IV to the notification number 5.0. 3289(E), dated the 247 September, 2020 by the 
Ministry of Jal Shakti shall be followed. 


(iii) Aadhaar Card or Pan Card or GST No. (as applicable) of the applicant and in the case of any 
registered society, trust, firm, company the resolution passed in General Body Meeting for extracting the 
water from the ground and authorisation to the concerned office bearer of the society. 


(2) Rain water harvesting process shall be followed as per the existing model Building Bye-laws made 
by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and a proposal to this effect shall be submitted to the 


Cantonment Board. 


Directions by Cantonment Board. — The Cantonment Board may issue directions to stop extraction of 
ground water at any time by recording reasons therefor. 


Levy of fee. - (1) If any registered user does not install the flow meter or in case flow meter is not working, 
the registration of such user may be suspended and the suspension may be revoked with an application by the 
user to the authority with a fee of rupees ten thousand. 


(2) Charges for residential bore well extraction above one thousand liters per day shall be charged at 


rupees five thousand per annum or as may be specified from time to time. 


(3) Charges for commercial or industrial bore well extraction above five hundred liters per day shall be 


charged at rupees ten thousand per annum or as may be specified from time to time. 


Restriction on use of water. — Ground water so extracted shall not be sold in any form by the applicant or 
any person without permission of the authority and if it is noticed that the applicant or any person is selling 
the extracted ground water without permission, the registration granted shall be suspended forthwith and bore 
well and the flow meter shall be sealed and the user shall be liable to pay fee up to rupees ten thousand or as 
may be specified from time to time. 


Protection of quality of ground water. — The applicant and user of the ground water shall be required to test 
the quality of the water in every three years from the Government Agency in order to ascertain as to whether 
the water is potable and submit the report to the authority and in case, water is found contaminated, the water 


shall not be used for drinking purpose. 


Rain water harvesting. — Every applicant has to ensure that rain water harvesting structures are erected and 
rain water harvesting is observed and the Cantonment Board shall ensure that rain water harvesting is 
functional and survey for verification of the same shall be conducted by the Cantonment Board from time to 


time.

16. Prohibitory orders. —The authority may issue prohibitory orders, in case it is found that the water is 
contaminated and injurious to human consumption by issuing notice to the user. 


17. Water audit. — Water audit shall be carried out by the authority from time to time and availability of the 
ground water shall be ascertained and in case of reduction in the ground water, restriction on the extraction of 
ground water shall be imposed as decided by the authority. 


18. Appeal. - (1) Every appeal against the decision of Chief Executive Officer shall be preferred before the 
Cantonment Board and the appeal against the decision of the Cantonment Board shall be preferred before the 
Principal Director, Defence Estates, the Command. 


(2) Every appeal shall be made within a period of thirty days from the date of communication of order 
of the Chief Executive Officer or the Cantonment Board, as the case may be.

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the [20 August, 2024 

59.0, 3279(E).—Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways, 233(E) Dated:7/0/2024 , published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub- 
section (ii) issued under sub-section (l) of section 3A of the National Highway Act, 956 (48 of 956) (hereinafter 
referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule 
annexed to the said notification for building (Construction of New Flyover at Pastikudi at Ch. 65/200 Km on NH-26 
for the year 2022-23), maintenance, management and operation of NH26 in the stretch of land at Km. !65/200 
(Tahasil Office, Kesinga) in the district of KALAHANDI in the state of ODISHA; 

And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in“The Times of 
India” dated 08.03.2024 and “The Prameya” dated 09.03.2024 ; under sub-section (3) of section 3A of the said Act; 

And whereas the Competent Authority has received objections filed under Section 3-C, considered and 
settled the same appropriately; 

And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (l) of section 3D of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 

Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (.) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 

And further, in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3D of the said Act, the Central Government hereby 
declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said Schedule shall 
vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी;

को fe गोवन', 'भंगर भुय' और 'पुढारी' में प्रकाशित किया गया था;

दिया है|

और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3डी की उप-धारा (1) के अनुसरण में, केंद्रीय सरकार को 
अपनी रिपोर्ट दे दी है; 


अतः, अब, केंद्रीय सरकार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी की उक्त रिपोर्ट प्राप्त हो जाने पर और उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3डी 
की उप - धारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह घोषणा करती है कि उक्त अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का 
पूर्वोक्त प्रयोजन के लिए अर्जन किया जाना चाहिए;

इस अधिसूचना के राजपत्र में प्रकाशन पर उक्त अनिसुचि में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि, सभी विल्लंगमों से मुक्त होकर आत्यंतिक रूप

MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
NOTIFICATION 
New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 


9.0. 3278(E).— Whereas by the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways number S.O.790(E), dated 197 February 2023, has been published in the Gazette of India, 
Extraordinary, Part II, section 3, Sub-section (ji) issued under sub-section (1) of section 3(A) of the National 
Highways Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government declared its 
intention to acquire the land specified in the Schedule annexed to the said notification for Land Acquisition for four 
laning of NH-748 from Km.97/00 to Km.112/00 on NH-748 in the state of Goa. 


And whereas the substance of the said notification has been published in “The Goan ” dated 22/2/2024; 
“Bhanagar Bhuin” and “Pudhari” dated 22/2/2024, under sub-section (3) of section 3(A) of the said Act; 


And whereas, objections have been received and the same have been considered by the competent authority; 


And whereas, in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3(D) of the said Act, the competent authority has 
submitted its report to the Central Government; 


Now, therefore, upon receipt of the said report of the competent authority and in exercise of the powers 
conferred by the sub-section (1) of section 3(D) of the said Act, the Central Government hereby declares that the land 
specified in the said Schedule should be acquired for the aforesaid purpose; 


And further, in pursuance of sub - section (2) of section 3 (D) of the said Act, the Central Government 
hereby declares that on publication of this notification in the Official Gazette, the land specified in the said 
Schedule shall vest absolutely in the Central Government, free from all encumbrances.

FTA. 3268(अ).--केन्द्रीय सरकार, राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग अधिनियम 1956 (1956 का 48) (जिसे इसमें इसके 
पश्चात्‌ उक्त अधिनियम कहा गया है) की धारा 3क की उप-धारा (1) द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग करते हुए, यह समाधान 
हो जाने के पश्चात्‌ कि तेलंगाना राज्य के नारायणपेट जिले में NH167 के कि.मी. 181.2 से कि.मी. 283 (कोल्लेकतोरते, 
नरायणपेट) NH167 के देओसुगुर (तेलंगाना/कनागटक बॉडगर) (कि.मी. 181.200) से जड्चर्ला (कि.मी. 283.000) के 
भू-खण्ड के 4-लेन का बनाना के के लोक प्रयोजन के लिए वह भूमि अपेक्षित है जिसका संक्षिप्त वर्णन नीचे अनुसूची में दिया 
गया है, ऐसी भूमि का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा करती है । 


कोई भी व्यक्ति, जो उक्त भूमि में हितबद्ध है, उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3ग की उप-धारा (1) के अधीन पूर्वोक्त 
प्रयोजन के लिए ऐसी भूमि के उपयोग पर राजपत्र में इस अधिसूचना के प्रकाशन की तारीख से इक्नकीस दिन के भीतर अपनी 
आपत्ति प्रकट कर सकेगा | 


ऐसी प्रत्येक आपत्ति सक्षम प्राधिकारी, अर्थात्‌ रेवेनुए डिविशनल अफसर, नरायणपेट को लिखित रूप में प्रस्तुत 
की जाएगी और उसमें उसके आधार अधिकथित किए जाएंगे और सक्षम प्राधिकारी, आपत्तिकर्ता को व्यक्तिगत रूप में या 
किसी विधिक पेशेवर द्वारा सुने जाने का अवसर देगा और ऐसी आपत्तियों की सुनवाई के पश्चात्‌ तथा ऐसी और जाँच करने 
के पश्चात्‌, यदि कोई हो, जिसे सक्षम प्राधिकारी आवश्यक समझे, आदेश द्वारा या तो आपत्तियों को अनुज्ञात कर सकेगा या 
अननुज्ञात कर सकेगा |

New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 


S.O. 3268(E).—In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that 
for the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for four 
laning of Deosugur (Telangana/Karnataka Border) (Km. 181.200) - Jadcherla (Km. 283.000) section of NH-167 as a 
part of Hyderabad - Panaji Corridor building (widening/two lane with paved shoulder/four laning etc.,), maintenance, 
management and operation of NH167 (Collectorate, Narayanpet) in the district of NARAYANPET in the state 
of TELANGANA, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Official Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(1) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, Revenue Divisional Officer, 
Narayanpet in writing and shall set out the grounds thereof and the Competent Authority shall give the objector an 
opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a legal practitioner, and may, after hearing all such objections and 
after making such further enquiry, if any, as the Competent Authority thinks necessary, by order, either allow or 
disallow the objections. 


Any order made by the Competent Authority under sub-section (2) of section 3C of the said Act shall be 
final. 


The land plans and other details of the land to be acquired under their notification are available and can be 
inspected by the interested person at the aforesaid office of the Competent Authority.

New Delhi, the 12th August, 2024 


S.O. 3270(E).—In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3A of the National Highways 
Act, 1956 (48 of 1956) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the Central Government, after being satisfied that for 
the public purpose, the land, the brief description of which is given in the Schedule below, is required for building 
Construction of Proposed ROB, RBK-21 at km 154.831 on NH-75E(New NH-20) in the stretch of land from 
km154.800 to km 156.625 (West Singhbhum, Chaibasa) in the district of WEST SINGHBHUM in the state of 
JHARKHAND, hereby declares its intention to acquire such land. 


Any person interested in the said land may, within twenty-one days from the date of publication of this 
notification in the Officia Gazette, object to the use of such land for the aforesaid purpose under sub-section(I) of 
section 3C of the said Act. 


Every such objection shall be made to the Competent Authority, namely, District Land Acquisition Officer in 
writing and shall set out the grounds thereof Competent Authority shall give the objector an opportunity of being

परिवहन और राजमार्ग मंत्रालय की अधिसूचना संख्या का.आ. 788(अ.) तारीख 49/02/2024, जो भारत के राजपत्र, 
असाधारण, भाग Ul, खण्ड 3, उपखंड (ii) H प्रकाशित की गई थी, ओडिशा राज्य में मयूरभंज जिले में एनएच-220 के 
कि.मी. 37.5 से कि.मी.38.5 रांची - विजयवाड़ा करिडोर पर रायरंगपुर में बाईपास रोड का निर्माण के लिए उस 
अधिसूचना से उपाबद्ध अनुसूची में विनिर्दिष्ट भूमि का अर्जन करने के अपने आशय की घोषणा की थी ; 


और उक्त अधिसूचना का सार उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3क की उपधारा (3) के अधीन तारीख "06.06.2024" 
को "धरित्रि - ओडिआ" और "आजिकालि - ओडिआ" दोनों में प्रकाशित किया गया था ; 


जबकि सक्षम प्राधिकारी को धारा 3-ग के तहत दायर आपत्ति प्राप्त हुई है, जिस पर विचार किया गया है और 
उसका उचित रूप से निपटान किया गया; 


और सक्षम प्राधिकारी ने उक्त अधिनियम की धारा 3घ की उपधारा (॥) के अनुसरण में, केन्द्रीय सरकार को अपनी 
रिपोर्ट दे दी है;
